report_name: AI Research Firm METR Discloses $600k API Key Theft

threat_actors.name: Financially Motivated Actor (March 2026)
threat_actors.description: An unnamed, financially motivated actor who stole a METR API key in March 2026 and used it to consume approximately $600,000 in AI credits for resource hijacking.

threat_actors.name: Unknown Attacker (May 2026)
threat_actors.description: An unknown threat actor who conducted a sustained, automated attack campaign against METR's public infrastructure in May 2026, involving scanning, credential stuffing, and phishing.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: An attacker stole an API key used for inference on public AI models, likely from a misconfigured server, public code repository, or a compromised developer machine.

attack_patterns.name: Resource Hijacking
attack_patterns.description: The stolen API key was used to consume approximately $600,000 in cloud computing resources for AI model inference, a form of resource hijacking.

attack_patterns.name: Active Scanning
attack_patterns.description: Attackers conducted systematic, automated scanning of METR's public infrastructure to probe for vulnerabilities.

attack_patterns.name: Password Spraying
attack_patterns.description: Attackers employed password spraying or credential stuffing attacks against METR's authentication providers.

attack_patterns.name: Credential Stuffing
attack_patterns.description: Attackers conducted credential stuffing attacks against METR's login portals as part of a sustained campaign.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: A phishing campaign was launched targeting METR staff as part of a multi-faceted attack.

campaigns.name: METR Probing Campaign (May 2026)
campaigns.description: A sustained, automated attack campaign in May 2026 targeting METR's public infrastructure, involving systematic scanning, credential stuffing, OAuth abuse attempts, and phishing.

identities.name: METR
identities.description: A non-profit AI safety research firm (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) that was the victim of two separate security incidents in March and May 2026, one involving API key theft and the other a sustained probing campaign.

infrastructure.name: Attacker Probing Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Automated infrastructure used in May 2026 to systematically scan METR's public-facing systems for vulnerabilities.

infrastructure.name: Compromised METR Asset
infrastructure.description: The source of the API key theft in March 2026, suggested by METR to be a misconfigured server, public code repository, or a compromised developer machine.

indicators.name: Potential Credential Stuffing or Password Spraying Attack
indicators.pattern:
title: High Rate of Authentication Failures
id: 2f8b5c1a-9d0e-4b3c-8a7f-1e2d3c4b5a6f
status: experimental
description: Detects a high rate of failed login attempts from a single source IP, which could indicate a password spraying or credential stuffing attack.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-steal-metr-api-key-and.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-01
tags:
  - attack.t1110.003
  - attack.t1110.004
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: azure
detection:
  selection:
    ResultType: '50126' # Error code for invalid credentials
  timeframe: 10m
  condition: selection | count() > 20 by ClientIP
indicators.description: Detects a high rate of failed logins, which can indicate password spraying or credential stuffing attacks, as seen in the May 2026 campaign against METR.

indicators.name: Cloud Cost Anomaly Indicating Resource Hijacking
indicators.pattern:
title: Cloud Cost Anomaly Detection
id: 8c1d9e2f-3b4a-4c5d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects a sudden and significant spike in cloud provider billing, which is a strong indicator of resource hijacking or fraudulent API key usage.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-steal-metr-api-key-and.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-01
tags:
  - attack.t1496
  - attack.impact
level: critical
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    # This is a conceptual rule. Real implementation would require a SIEM with cost data integration or a dedicated cloud cost management tool.
    # The logic is to detect an unusual increase in API calls that incur high costs, such as starting many GPU instances.
    eventName: RunInstances
    requestParameters.instanceType|startswith: 
      - 'p4'
      - 'p5'
      - 'g5'
      - 'g6'
  timeframe: 1h
  condition: selection | count() > 5
indicators.description: Detects a sudden, massive spike in cloud spending, which is a primary indicator of resource hijacking, as seen in the March 2026 incident at METR.
